title: Why you see faces in everyday objects, like electrical sockets
hook: Ever notice a face staring back from an electrical socket?

narration.text: Your brain is hardwired to find faces, even in random patterns.
This phenomenon is called pareidolia, where the brain interprets vague stimuli as something familiar.
It is an evolutionary trait, helping us quickly recognise other humans.
We are especially sensitive to features like two eyes and a mouth.
Even with just a few dots and lines, our brain completes the picture.
This means you might see a happy car grille or a surprised mop.
It is a glimpse into how our perception shapes reality.
What is the funniest face you have seen in an everyday object?

description: Discover why your brain is constantly finding faces in inanimate objects. Learn about pareidolia and its evolutionary roots, explaining why you see eyes and mouths everywhere.
topic: Why you sometimes see faces in everyday objects, like electrical sockets.
